svg.text: Two shelves and a slip of paper
Concept 2 · Node 1's 4 MB flash map, the Minimal SPIFFS scheme (min_spiffs.csv, esp32 package 3.3.12)
The 4 MB flash, drawn to scale
the first 64 KB: the shelf opener, the partition table, nvs, otadata (zoomed in below)
Node 1 1.7.0 = 1,411,683 bytes (71% of a shelf; the author's compile)
Node 1 1.6.0 = 1,194,928 bytes (60% of a shelf; Module 21)
nvs: Wi-Fi, the device key, thresholds,
by an update or a rollback
otadata = a slip of paper: which shelf
Three states during the Module 28 practice
the shelf opener (bootloader) reads otadata at every start, then runs the shelf it points to
installed by cable: no trial period
A cable upload writes the shelf opener 0x1000,
and app0: the board always goes back to app0
the last firmware that must go by cable:
below 1.7.0 there is no trial period yet
the download goes to the other shelf (app1);
the first 16 bytes are written last, only then
otadata points to app1: a half-written shelf
the other shelf of app1 = app0: 1.7.0 overwritten
by 1.7.2; that firmware fails to prove itself
Uploaded to the server: node-1-home.ino.bin (first byte 0xE9, one shelf), not .merged.bin (4 MB, starts at address 0x0) or .bootloader.bin
File limit = one shelf, 1,966,080 bytes; ESP.getFreeSketchSpace() answers the size of the other shelf, not the free space left
A spare shelf needs a two-shelf scheme (Module 10); the scheme without OTA (No OTA, Huge APP): the command is accepted, then the update failed (Update 10)
